title: AES Encryption
subtitle: Advanced Encryption Standard: blocks, keys, and rounds

content.text: AES is the standard symmetric block cipher, used everywhere from TLS to full-disk encryption. It operates on 128-bit blocks and supports 128, 192, or 256-bit keys.

content.code:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import Cipher, algorithms, modes
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend
import os

key = os.urandom(32)   # AES-256 key
iv  = os.urandom(16)   # Initialisation vector

# Encrypt
cipher = Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), modes.CBC(iv), backend=default_backend())
enc = cipher.encryptor()
ciphertext = enc.update(b"Hello, AES-CBC!  ") + enc.finalize()  # must be 16-byte aligned

# Decrypt
dec = cipher.decryptor()
plaintext = dec.update(ciphertext) + dec.finalize()
print(plaintext)

content.text: AES-CBC requires a unique random IV for every encryption. Never reuse an IV with the same key.

questions.question: What block size does AES use?
questions.explanation: AES always operates on 128-bit (16-byte) blocks regardless of key length.

faq.q: Should I use AES-CBC in new code?
faq.a: Prefer AES-GCM (authenticated encryption). AES-CBC does not authenticate the ciphertext, so an attacker can tamper with it undetected.
